tasks.q: Which data type should store the price 4.99?
tasks.fb: A real number can hold a decimal part, and an integer cannot.

tasks.q: Which data type can hold only two possible values?
tasks.fb: A Boolean is either True or False, and nothing else.

a: Converting a value from one data type to another
Rounding a number to the nearest whole number
Giving a variable a new name
Copying a value into a constant
tasks.fb: The data type changes. Casting is not the same thing as rounding.

tasks.q: What is the value of  int("25") + 5 ?
a: An error, because you cannot add to a string
tasks.fb: int() turns the string "25" into the number 25, so ordinary arithmetic then works.

tasks.q: In the OCR Exam Reference Language, what is the value of  5 ^ 2 ?
tasks.fb: The exponent operator raises 5 to the power 2, so the answer is 5 x 5.
Multiplication happens before addition, so 3 * 4 is worked out first.

tasks.q: What is the value of  23 MOD 4 ?
tasks.fb: 4 goes into 23 five times with 3 left over, and MOD gives that remainder.

tasks.q: What is the value of  23 DIV 4 ?
tasks.fb: DIV gives only the whole number of times 4 goes into 23 and ignores the remainder.

tasks.q: age = 15. What is the result of  age >= 13 AND age <= 19 ?
a: An error, because two conditions cannot be tested at once
tasks.fb: Both conditions are True, and AND needs both sides to be True.

tasks.q: day = "Sat". What is the result of  day == "Sat" OR day == "Sun" ?
a: An error, because OR only works with numbers
tasks.fb: OR needs only one side to be True, and the first comparison is True.

tasks.q: name = "Hazel". In the OCR Exam Reference Language, what does  name.substring(0, 3)  give?
tasks.fb: It starts at position 0, the first character, and takes three characters from there.

tasks.q: In the OCR Exam Reference Language, ASC("A") returns 65. What does  CHR(66)  return?
tasks.fb: CHR converts an ASCII code back into a character, and 66 is one more than the code for A.

tasks.q: Match each expression to its value.
tasks.fb: MOD and DIV are the two most often muddled: DIV is how many times it goes in, MOD is what is left over.

tasks.q: Which expression gives the remainder when 30 is divided by 7?
tasks.fb: MOD gives the remainder, which here is 2, because 7 goes into 30 four times with 2 left over.

tasks.q: Boxes hold 12 eggs. Fill in the two blanks on each row.
tasks.fb: DIV is how many whole boxes you fill, MOD is what is left over on the bench. The last row is the one worth remembering: 7 DIV 12 is 0, because you cannot fill a box at all, and 7 MOD 12 is the whole 7.

info.title: Why types matter
info.text: Choosing the right data type saves memory and prevents errors. A Boolean needs only one bit of information, while storing the same yes or no as a string needs a byte for every character.

info.title: Casting can lose data
info.text: Casting a real number to an integer throws the decimal part away rather than rounding it, so 4.9 becomes 4. If you need rounding, use a rounding function instead of a cast.

info.title: Integer division
info.text: Dividing with / can give an answer with a decimal part even when both numbers are whole. That is exactly why DIV exists: it keeps the answer a whole number.

info.title: MOD in the real world
info.text: MOD is how programs wrap around. hours MOD 24 keeps a clock in range, and index MOD listLength cycles through a list for ever without ever running off the end.

info.title: Short circuits
info.text: Many languages stop evaluating an AND as soon as one side is found to be False, because the final answer cannot change. This is called short-circuit evaluation and it saves time.

info.title: ASCII
info.text: ASCII gives every character a number: capital A is 65, lower case a is 97 and the digit 0 is 48. Because the codes run in order, the gap between a capital and its lower case letter is always 32.

diagrams.title: Inside a string
diagrams.text: Every character has a position, counted from 0. See length, a substring taken from a position, upper and lower case, and two strings joined.
